data.name: AproposD2
data.value: The Agency and its mechanism have recently undergone significant and important developments, reflecting a series of reforms aimed at a radical shift from a purely administrative approach in processing files to a coherent economic approach, in addition to improving efficiency and performance in management, particularly regarding financial risk management, as well as raising awareness of entrepreneurial thinking and enhancing the skills and competencies of young people. The aim is to encourage the creation of high-performing micro-enterprises that are resilient and generate sustainable added value in the national economy.

data.name: AproposD3
data.value: The National Entrepreneurship Support and Development Agency comprises 51 wilaya agencies, as well as many branches distributed across the national territory, with more than 170 local branches. In addition, there are presence points through more than 200 Entrepreneurship Development Centers, distributed across various universities, institutes, and schools in the higher education sector, as well as institutes and institutions in the vocational education and training sector.

data.name: Aproposdetails
data.value: The National Entrepreneurship Support and Development Agency is a government body of a special nature, placed under the tutelage of the Ministry of Knowledge Economy, Start-ups, and Micro-Enterprises. It manages a mechanism with an economic approach, aimed at supporting project holders in creating and expanding micro-enterprises in the production of goods and services, with the goal of generating wealth and sustainable employment opportunities. The Agency’s tasks focus on the following core activities

data.name: ButProgrammeDesc1
data.value: The program is based on a holistic approach that brings together the various stakeholders of the local entrepreneurial ecosystem: the Wilaya, the Commune, decentralized services, and the relevant bodies and institutions. The success of the program depends on the combined efforts of all local development actors, in order to implement the directives of the President of the Republic, Mr. Abdelmadjid Tebboune, aimed at creating 450,000 jobs and establishing sustainable local development, with the goal of reaching the year 2027, which will be a decisive milestone for Algeria, marked by the completion of the digitization process and the reaping of the benefits of developing the national economy.

data.name: ButProgrammeDesc2
data.value: Promoting local micro-enterprises means enhancing the national production value chain and paving the way towards self-sufficiency, in order to achieve “Algerian production for Algerians.”

data.name: CadreProgramme1
data.value: The program implements the commitments of the President of the Republic, Mr. Abdelmadjid Tebboune, to develop a “new economic model based on diversified growth and the knowledge economy.” These commitments stem from his dedication and interest in youth, the promotion of entrepreneurship among them, and his support for their projects.

data.name: CadreProgramme2
data.value: It translates his high-level directives aimed at meeting the challenge of economic recovery by building a productive and diversified economy that creates value and quality and sustainable local development.

data.name: CadreProgramme3
data.value: The program also contributes to strengthening the role of local authorities as a driving force for national development.

data.name: DefinitionProgrammeImpact70P1
data.value: This is the new program of the National Entrepreneurship Support and Development Agency (NESDA) for micro-enterprises interested in local development, called IMPACT 70.

data.name: DefinitionProgrammeImpact70P2
data.value: The name derives from the impact that a micro-enterprise has on its environment: economic (creating added value, processing raw materials, etc.), social (job creation, local services, etc.), and individual (self-fulfillment, entrepreneurship, etc.). The number 70 commemorates the anniversary of the outbreak of the glorious November 1, 1954 Revolution, which coincided with the launch of the program.

data.name: DescriptionFG
data.value: The Mutual Caution Fund to Guarantee Credits Risks of the Project Holders works to cover the risks associated with bank loans granted to micro-enterprises financed within the framework of the National Entrepreneurship Support and Development Agency. The fund constitutes a complementary guarantee for banks, in addition to the guarantees provided by micro-enterprises, which contributes to strengthening banks’ confidence in financing entrepreneurial projects.

data.name: organisationNesdaText
data.value: In accordance with the provisions of Executive Decree n °96-296 dated 24 Rabi' al-Thani 1417, corresponding to September 8, 1996, as amended and supplemented, which established the National Entrepreneurship Support and Development Agency and defined its statutes, the agency is governed by a board of directors and managed by a director general, and is also equipped with a supervisory committee.

data.name: Partenaire1P1
data.value: Partnership with institutions in the higher education and scientific research sector, under the supervision of the tutelage ministry, falls within the framework of opening Entrepreneurship Development Centers across the university network. The goal is to coordinate their management and organize training sessions, conducted jointly by university professors and trainers from the Agency according to the planned work programs.

data.name: Partenaire1P2
data.value: These Entrepreneurship Development Centers play a vital role in promoting entrepreneurship in universities through training, awareness, and support activities they provide.

data.name: Partenaire2P1
data.value: In order to expand the experience of Entrepreneurship Development Centers to the network of education and vocational training institutions, this partnership, under the supervision of the tutelage ministry, aims to coordinate the opening of these Centers, regulate their management, organize training sessions, in addition to training trainers from the sector with the support of Agency trainers.

data.name: Partenaire2P2
data.value: These centers are considered a key factor in promoting entrepreneurial thinking and entrepreneurship within education and vocational training through their training, awareness, and support activities.

data.name: Partenaire3P1
data.value: The partnership with public banking institutions falls within the framework of the Agency’s mechanism and is reflected in the triangular financing structure, under which the bank loan represents 70% of the investment, in addition to a 100% rebate interest bank. This acts as an incentive to create micro-enterprises and expanding their activities.

data.name: Partenaire3P2
data.value: Bank financing plays a pivotal role in the Agency’s mechanism due to its importance in the process of setting up micro-enterprises and expanding their activities.

data.name: Partenaire4P1
data.value: Within the framework of accompanying micro-enterprises and supporting their activities, the Agency collaborates with both public and private economic operators to promote goods and services of micro-enterprises and the advantages they provide through the economic value chain, including supplying inputs, auxiliary services, and subcontracting.

data.name: Partenaire4P2
data.value: These partnerships allow micro-enterprises to get closer to economic operators, exchange expertise, and exploit business opportunities from supplying raw materials to subcontracting certain activities.

data.name: Partenaire4P3
data.value: In this regard, the Agency ensures the signing of partnership agreements with various economic operators, with several agreements concluded at the local and national levels, including:

data.name: Partenaire4P3,1
data.value: Regional branches of the Algerian Economic Renewal Council

data.name: Partenaire4P3,2
data.value: National Fund for Agricultural Cooperation

data.name: Partenaire4P3,3

data.name: Partenaire4P3,4
data.value: Algerian Water Company

data.name: Partenaire4P3,5
data.value: Local economic companies in the food industry, manufacturing, and services

data.name: Partenaire5P1
data.value: To ensure continuous coordination with various public institutions and bodies involved in supporting micro-enterprises throughout their creation and operation, and in order to establish a stimulating entrepreneurial ecosystem that fosters opportunities. The Agency aims through these partnerships to simplify and improve procedures, exchange experiences and data, and coordinate activities, especially those related to awareness, communication, and support, in accordance with the legislation and regulations in force.

data.name: ProgCoopérationsText
data.value: Within the framework of promoting the entrepreneurship spirit and strengthen the skills of microenterprises, the National Entrepreneurship Support and Development Agency is committed to enhancing its capacities by establishing cooperation ties with various accredited international and regional bodies, to benefit from expertise and experiences, as well as to expand opportunities for exchange and innovation. The Agency contributes as an important partner in many international cooperation programs in Algeria.

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre1TextP1
data.value: This regional program aims to support youth entrepreneurship in the agricultural sector by enabling young people to develop new, innovative, and sustainable projects that can create employment opportunities in promising agricultural sectors in Algeria.

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre1TextP2
data.value: The program is implemented by the International Labour Organization (ILO) and funded by the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) of the United Nations Organization, with oversight from the relevant ministerial sectors. The Agency is a key partner in this program, alongside the National Office for Rural Development Studies (BNEDER), the public accelerator A-Venture, the National Agency for Microcredit Management (ANGEM), and the National Employment Agency (ANEM).

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre1TextP3
data.value: In 2024, the Agency contributed to organizing a business plan competition targeting project owners, enabling them to enhance their entrepreneurial skills and launch economically viable activities in the agricultural sector, predefined according to value chains: potatoes in Mostaganem, aquaculture in Biskra and dairy production in Guelma. Participants also benefited from technical support to develop a viable business plan and finance their projects, depending on the situation.

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre1TextP4
data.value: The program witnessed significant participation, unveiling several innovative project ideas. Participants benefited training sessions that strengthened their capacities in preparing business plans, improved their entrepreneurial skills, and their experience in the targeted agricultural field. The program also honored the top winners from the three concerned wilayas, who will benefit from the Agency’s support to create their microenterprises.

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre2TextP1
data.value: The program is a regional project of the International Labour Organization (ILO), funded by the Directorate-General for Neighborhood policy and Enlargement Negotiations (DG NEAR) at the European Commission, and supports the transition from the informal to the formal economy through tripartite social dialogue in Arab countries, with a special focus on Algeria, Egypt, Lebanon, and Palestine.

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre2TextP2
data.value: The project aims to increase employment for workers and the productivity of enterprises in the formal sector, which contributes to decent work for all, poverty reduction, and the building of more equitable and cohesive societies. To achieve this, the program seeks to strengthen the capacities of the ILO’s tripartite constituents: governments, employers’ organizations, and workers’ organizations, to act through social dialogue at two main levels:

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre2TextP3
data.value: Developing comprehensive policies for the transition to the formal economy

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre2TextP4
data.value: Developing national training systems and skills recognition, with a focus on youth and women in the informal sector

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre3TextP1
data.value: The “Social and Solidarity Economy for Sustainable Economic Inclusion of Youth Entrepreneurs in Algeria” program aims to encourage youth employment and contribute to wealth creation through establishing a supportive ecosystem for the development of the social and solidarity economy (SSE).

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre3TextP2
data.value: To achieve this, the project includes several key components, each operating at different levels of this ecosystem and targeting the various stakeholders involved, focusing on two main objectives:

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre3TextP3
data.value: Strengthening the social and solidarity economy ecosystem

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre3TextP4
data.value: Supporting the creation and development of social and solidarity economy enterprises

data.name: ProgCoopérationsTitre3TextP5
data.value: The program operates under the auspices of the United Nations Development Program (UNDP) and the supervision of relevant ministerial sectors, where the Agency acts as a key partner, it contributes to accompanying the creation and expansion of microenterprise projects within the social and solidarity economy in line with the defined objectives.

data.name: TaxDescription
data.value: The project owner benefits from tax privileges during the phases of establishing the project and expanding its production capacity, which helps reduce financial burdens and encourages investment in various economic projects.

data.name: TaxPhase1,1
data.value: Exemption from property transfer duties for real estate acquisitions made for a financial consideration within the framework of creating an industrial activity.

data.name: TaxPhase1,2
data.value: Exemption from value-added tax (VAT) on the acquisition of equipment and services that are directly involved in the implementation of the investment during both the establishment and expansion phases, for activities subject to the real tax system. (Passenger vehicles are excluded from this measure unless they constitute the main tool of the activity).

data.name: TaxPhase1,3
data.value: Application of a reduced 5% customs duty rate on imported equipment directly used in the implementation of the investment.

data.name: TaxPhase2,1
data.value: Exemption from property tax on buildings and additional constructions for 3, 6 or 10 years, depending on the project's location, starting from the date of completion.

data.name: TaxPhase2,2
data.value: Exemption from the single lump-sum tax (IFU) or, as applicable, from Corporate Income Tax (IBS) or Personal Income Tax (IRG) for a period of 3, 6, or 10 years, depending on the project’s location, starting from the date operation.

data.name: TaxPhase2,3
data.value: Upon expiration of the exemption period mentioned above, it may be extended for 2 years when the investor undertakes to employ at least 3 workers on a permanent basis.
